sentences.text:
2.  The main contention of the counsel appearing for the claimants is that deceased Pandurang @
Pandu, who was aged about 39 years as per Ex.P.5 - post mortem report and he was working as sugarcane cutter and his income was `15,000/- per month.
But, the Tribunal committed an error in taking his income at `6,000/- per month.
3. The counsel also would contend that Tribunal committed an error in deducting only 1/4th towards personal expenses and ought to have deducted 1/5th, since there were seven dependants.
The future prospects at 40% is also not awarded.

4. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for respondent would contend that the Tribunal rightly NC:
2025:KHC-K:4529-DB HC-KAR deducted 1/4th, since one of the daughter is already married and she cannot be termed as dependant.
5. He further submits that the Tribunal rightly taken the income and also awarded the same.

Hence,
the award does not require any interference.

6. Having heard the learned counsel appearing for the appellants as well as the counsel for respondent, the points that would arise for consideration are :
i) Whether the Tribunal committed an error in awarding just and reasonable compensation?
ii) Whether it requires any interference of this Court ?
7.
It is not in dispute that accident had taken place on 10.05.2015 and also the specific case of the claimants is that deceased was working as sugarcane cuter.

When the accident taken place in the year 2015, Tribunal ought to have taken the income of `8,000/- per month in view of the chart prepared by the Karnataka NC: 2025:KHC-K:4529-DB HC-KAR State Legal Services Authorities,
but committed an error in taking the same at `6,000/-.

Nagamma And Ors vs The Divisional Controller on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181059567/
3 8. There is a force in the contention of the counsel appearing for the appellants regarding deduction.

sentences.text: The Tribunal ought to considered the deduction at 1/5th instead of 1/4th, even though the claimants are wife and six children and no doubt one of the daughter was married, but in view of the recent decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Seema Rani and Ors. V. Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. and Ors.1, it is categorically held that in view of decision in the case of National Insurance Company Limited v. Birendra and Ors.2, married daughter also comes within the purview of dependant.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: When such being the case, the contention of the counsel appearing for the respondent-Corporation cannot be accepted.
There is force in the contention of the counsel appearing for the appellants that Tribunal ought to have deducted only 1/5th towards personal expenses of deceased.
The Tribunal also not awarded any future prospects and the fact that deceased was 39 years old as per Ex.P.5 - post mortem report are not in dispute.
10. When such being the case, this Court has to revisit the calculation.
Having considered the notional income as `8,000/-, by adding 40% as future prospects, it comes to `11,200/-.
Having considered the same i.e., `11,200/- by deducting 1/5th towards personal incomes it comes to `8,960/-.

The loss of dependency comes to `16,12,800/- (`8,960/- x 12 x 15).
11.
The fact that there are seven dependants, loss of consortium would be `40,000/- x 7, it would be `2,80,000/-.
Apart from that, to Rs.15,000/- is awarded towards funeral expenses and transportation expenses.
Also at `15,000/- towards loss of estate.
Thus, total compensation comes to `19,22,800/-.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:4529-DB HC-KAR 12.

Since more than six years have lapsed after rendering of decision in National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Ors.3, appellants would be entitled for addition of 20% i.e.,
`62,000/- on award under conventional heads.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi and Ors.3
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Adding the same, it comes to `19,84,800/- and same is payable with interest at the rate of 6% and hence, we have answered the points as affirmative in coming to the conclusion that Tribunal committed an error in not awarding just and reasonable compensation.

In view of discussion made above, we pass the following :
ORDER i) Appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The judgment and award dated 18.03.2019 passed in MVC No.1150/2015 by the Court of the I Additional Senior Civil Judge and Member, MACT, Vijayapur is modified by granting compensation of `19,84,800/- as against `8,90,000/- with interest of 6% (2017) 16 SCC 680 NC: 2025:KHC-K:4529-DB HC-KAR from the date of petition except for delayed period of 283 days vide order dated 07.08.2025.
Nagamma And Ors vs The Divisional Controller on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/181059567/
4 iii)
Enhanced compensation is payable within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
iv) The disbursement of the amount is unaltered.
